children: Quess Corp report finds a 4.5 percentage point rise in demand for advanced technology skills in Q2 FY27, while tier II cities gain momentum

Artificial intelligence (AI), data and cybersecurity accounted for 30.3 per cent of technology hiring demand at India's Global Capability Centres (GCCs) in the July-September quarter of 2026, up from 25.8 per cent in the preceding quarter, according to a report by Quess Corp. The findings point to a growing focus on specialised technology skills, even as talent shortages and concentration of advanced-skill hiring in major cities remain challenges.

The India GCC Tech Talent Landscape – Q2 FY27 Report identifies supply gaps of 38-42 per cent in AI, data and analytics, and 30-35 per cent in cybersecurity and risk management. It also found that 87-88 per cent of advanced-skill hiring remained concentrated in tier I cities.

The report recorded a 4.5 percentage point quarter-on-quarter increase in the combined share of AI, data and cybersecurity in technology hiring demand. The trend reflects GCCs' growing need for professionals who can deploy AI applications, manage data infrastructure and strengthen enterprise security.

Quess Corp identified transitions from adjacent roles as one way to address talent shortages. These include data scientists moving into model operations, data engineers shifting towards applied AI and cybersecurity analysts developing expertise in cloud security.
Structured reskilling and internal career pathways could complement external recruitment as demand for advanced technology capabilities expands across sectors, the report said.

Coimbatore recorded approximately 30 per cent quarter-on-quarter growth in GCC technology hiring demand during the July-September quarter. The city contributed to overall tier II hiring growth of 13 per cent, compared with 8-10 per cent in the first quarter of FY27.
The findings indicate that smaller cities are gaining traction in technology recruitment, although the bulk of demand remains concentrated in established hubs.
Among tier I cities, Pune was the only market to record growth, with hiring demand increasing by 2 per cent quarter-on-quarter. Other major metropolitan markets experienced declines.

Hyderabad and Mumbai recorded the steepest falls, at approximately 10 per cent and 9 per cent, respectively. Despite the contraction, tier I cities continued to account for around 84-86 per cent of total GCC hiring demand.

The report highlights the need to combine specialised recruitment with workforce development to address persistent skill gaps. Internal mobility and targeted training could help organisations build capabilities while reducing dependence on an already constrained external talent pool.

Quess Corp Chief Executive Officer – IT Staffing Kapil Joshi said India's GCC ecosystem was expanding while the skills required by companies were changing, with AI, data and cybersecurity accounting for 30.3 per cent of technology hiring demand in the second quarter of FY27.
The report draws on secondary data, job postings across multiple employment platforms and information available in the public domain.
